prompt:
You are a blind code reader in an empirical software-engineering study. Work only from the files in the current directory.

1. Read protocol.md first.
2. Read batch.md. It names 20 Java files by id, their path in their repository, and their local copy under files/.
3. For every file: read the whole file (use Read with offset and limit for files over 2000 lines, do not skip the tail). Identify the method with the highest cognitive complexity (the one with the most and deepest nested branches, loops and boolean chains) and name it. Then answer Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4 from the protocol as true or false, each with one sentence of evidence from the file, and write a one-line note of the form "methodName: what it does". Do NOT derive or state the category; the mapping is applied later.
4. Blindness: do not try to read anything outside the current directory and do not try to find out anything about these classes beyond the file itself.
5. Answer with one entry per id of the batch, all 20 of them, in the required JSON form.

evidence.q4: Complexity is nested loops and if/else over ranges, not a switch over cases.

readings.note: modifyAlignedChunkMetaData: applies time/value column modifications to aligned chunk metadata and removes chunks whose rows are all deleted

evidence.q1: transform (lines 104-149) splits the selected text into lines, runs each through the compiled grep filter and assembles the matching (and optionally non-matching) lines into the returned string.
evidence.q2: The class is one editor action that greps the selection according to dialog settings; the nested MyGrepFilter and handler serve that action.
evidence.q3: It reads its own GrepSettings value object and the editor text; no getter chains or field copying on other behaviour-bearing objects.
evidence.q4: Complexity is if/else with loops and nested blank checks, not a case dispatch.

readings.note: transform: filters text lines by the grep pattern, optionally grouping matches above non-matches

evidence.q1: processMethods (lines 248-372) loops the class file's methods and, per method, calls Ropper.convert, Optimizer.optimize, LocalVariableExtractor.extract, RopTranslator.translate and out.addDirectMethod/addVirtualMethod; it mainly decides which of these to call rather than computing a value itself.
evidence.q2: All methods serve translating a Java class file into a dex ClassDefItem (fields, methods, constants).
evidence.q3: It reads access flags and options from Method/CfOptions inputs and builds new EncodedMethod objects; there are no deep getter chains or field copying between other objects (the one depth-2 chain is to build a name string).
evidence.q4: Complexity is the per-method try block with nested if/else guards and boolean chains, not a switch over cases.

readings.note: processMethods: converts each class-file method to ROP, optionally optimises, translates to Dalvik code and adds it to the output class

evidence.q1: batchReplaceMetadata (lines 192-220) merges present topics with DB rows via TopicConverter and calls topicDAO.insert/updateById/deleteById; it forwards to the DAO rather than computing a result.
evidence.q2: All methods are topic lookups and updates across Kafka, ZooKeeper, DB and cache for the one TopicService contract.
evidence.q3: It works on Topic/TopicPO data objects and ClusterPhy fields that are plain entities, and delegates to DAOs; no behaviour from other classes is re-implemented here.
evidence.q4: Complexity is a loop with try/catch and if/else-if on nullness and equality, not a case table.

readings.note: batchReplaceMetadata: upserts current topics into the DB and deletes DB topics no longer present

evidence.q1: equals (lines 172-214) computes equality from the config's own twelve fields through a chain of null-safe comparisons.
evidence.q2: The class is a single code-generator configuration holder with getters/setters, defaults, equals/hashCode/toString.
evidence.q3: It only reads its own fields and those of another CodeGeneratorConfig of the same class.
evidence.q4: The complexity is a sequence of if-return-false comparisons, not a switch over one controlling value.

readings.note: equals: null-safe field-by-field equality of two CodeGeneratorConfig objects

evidence.q1: concatenateLineStrings (lines 107-136) iterates coordinate sequences, skips a first coordinate that duplicates the previous line's last one, and builds the merged LineString; a geometry routine over its inputs.
evidence.q2: All methods are static geometry helpers (line strings, splitting, GeoJSON conversion, distances) for the street module.
evidence.q3: It works on JTS geometry and GeoJSON value objects and produces new geometry; no behaviour from other classes is re-implemented.
evidence.q4: convertGeoJsonToJtsGeometry has an instanceof chain, but the most complex method's nesting is loops with && conditions, not a case table.

readings.note: concatenateLineStrings: joins several LineStrings into one, dropping duplicated joint coordinates

evidence.q1: yield() of the sliding-time-window reader (lines 178-292) pulls columns from the parent reader into its tvList and advances cached begin/end cursors with nested while loops to compute the next window's index range.
evidence.q2: The class builds row-window readers (sliding size, sliding time, session, state) over a single input column for one intermediate layer.
evidence.q3: It reads Column values and its own ElasticSerializableTVList; the parent reader is consumed as an input source, not decided upon by its fields.
evidence.q4: Complexity is nested while loops and index arithmetic, not a switch over cases.

readings.note: constructRowSlidingTimeWindowReader.yield: fetches data until the next time window is covered and computes the window's begin/end indices
